name: Opunake Surf Reef (North Reef)
coords: metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward the cove headland side referred to in sources as the reef's flank, true compass direction not published — treated as arbitrary +x); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0

crest_depth_m.datum: unknown — no datum stated in any accessible source; treat as approximate depth below mean sea level

distance_offshore_m.measured_from: shoreline (estimated centroid distance, not a surveyed figure)

orientation_notes: No plan-view figure, survey drawing or compass bearing for the Opunake reef was found in any accessible source (R1-R12 in the card, nor Gemini's cited-but-inaccessible 'Mead & Black 2007 Design Dossier' / 'Taranaki Regional Council Monitoring Records 2010'). The polygon here is a SCHEMATIC placeholder only: a symmetric isosceles wedge with its 20 m base at the shoreward (inshore) end and its apex pointing offshore (seaward), by direct analogy to the one Opunake-designer reef whose plan geometry IS described in a primary source in our reference list — Mount Maunganui, built by the same firm (ASR Ltd) around the same time, explicitly described as having its 'apex... point[ing] seaward and the structure thicken[ing] towards the base' [R3]. Opunake's own sources (R2, R4) state only that the reef's bags 'cover an area around 90m long and 20m wide' with no shape description; R2/R4 also both note the design was for a single 'right-hand wave' (one peel direction), unlike Mount Maunganui's two-directional wave off a symmetric V — meaning the real Opunake reef almost certainly had an ASYMMETRIC wedge/arm (like the 'asymmetric polygonal wedge' shape of the comparable Cables Reef), not the symmetric triangle drawn here. We chose the symmetric schematic deliberately rather than inventing a specific asymmetric skew, because no source gives which flank was the long peeling shoulder or the arm's angle to the shoreline. Distance offshore and crest depth are both low-confidence estimates (see derivation) since neither figure is published for Opunake specifically in any source we could access.
materials: 27 sand-filled geotextile ('geo-container') bags [R2][R4] (card). CORRECTED 2026-09-25: the fabric spec 'non-woven, polyester/polyester-polypropylene' previously cited to [R2][R4] does not appear in either source's text (re-fetched in full); that exact material description is R3's account of Mount Maunganui's bags, not Opunake's, and was misattributed. Opunake's own bag fabric composition is not published in any source we could access.

Kept the ~2.5 m figure since it is within the same order of magnitude and the crest-depth estimate already carries a ±1.0 m error bar that absorbs this.

disagree.ours: Schematic single-arm wedge, apex offshore, orientation/compass bearing unknown
disagree.why_ours: No source we could access (including Gemini's own two cited sources, which we could not locate or access) actually describes Opunake's arm as running along a rocky headland or gives its compass bearing. Gemini's 'cove headland alignment' narrative appears to be an unsourced elaboration built to explain away the 30x67 vs 80x30 discrepancy, not an independently documented fact.

open_issues: No primary source with an actual plan-view drawing, survey, or CAD figure for the Opunake reef was found or was accessible (NZ Geographic R3's full text has no figures/images at all and does not contain the 90x20 figure; ResearchGate R9 is blocked by Cloudflare on both WebFetch and curl, exactly as already flagged in the card).

The card's citation of the 90x20 footprint as [R2][R3][R4] is only fully supported by R2 and R4; R3's accessible text does not contain this figure. Worth a small correction pass on the card/dossier (not made here, per the task's Gemini-folder read-only / no-new-facts-into-card-without-a-separate-pass convention) — flagging it here as an open issue instead.

Crest depth and distance offshore are not published anywhere we could find for Opunake specifically; both values here are low-confidence estimates, clearly separable in the JSON from the two solidly-sourced dimensions (90 m / 20 m).

The true left/right asymmetry of the reef (it produced only a right-hand wave, unlike the symmetric two-directional Mount Maunganui V) is not captured by the symmetric schematic polygon used here, because no source specifies the arm's actual skew or compass angle.

Gemini's two cited sources for its dimensions ('Mead & Black 2007 Design Dossier', 'Taranaki Regional Council Environmental Monitoring Records 2010') could not be located or accessed by us at all -- not on ResearchGate, not via a direct fetch, not anywhere in either project's folders -- so Gemini's numbers could not be confirmed at the source and are not adopted, per project rule.
